follow_ups.title: T10 pins commit-failure behavior opposite to spec section A
follow_ups.detail: The spec says any runReview failure leaves the receipt unwritten and the next review re-runs. T10 instead requires a receipt to survive commit failure and the next review to return cached. Revise T10 to remove/rollback the receipt on commit failure, or obtain a spec amendment before execution.

follow_ups.title: T1 does not verify all seven identity fields
follow_ups.detail: TestFollowUpKeyIsInjective only exercises delimiter/quote collisions in file and title. An implementation omitting gate, wave, task, severity, or line could pass all declared tests and collapse unrelated findings. Add table tests mutating each tuple element independently, distinguishing nil wave from wave 0, and proving string trimming normalization.

follow_ups.title: Two-layers design still documents FollowUp.Wave as a plain int and the file as un-de-duplicated
follow_ups.detail: §5.4 says `gate.FollowUp gains Wave int and Task int, both omitempty` and "Append-only and un-de-duplicated as before; #44 is untouched by this design and gets more to de-duplicate." The diff (task 1, closing #44) changes `Wave` to `*int` (so wave 0 round-trips distinctly from no wave) and makes `AppendFollowUps` idempotent with an upgrade rule. The doc's own phrasing anticipated a later change would supersede this, but as written it now describes a shape and behaviour that no longer exist and isn't flagged as superseded.

follow_ups.title: Task 5 (goal-assessor citation validation, #24) is entirely absent from the reviewed diff
follow_ups.detail: None of task 5's required changes appear anywhere in wave-0.s1.a1.diff: no internal/finish/goals.go CheckCitations addition, no internal/cli/cmd_record.go readVerdicts root-param wiring, no internal/brief/templates/goal-assessor.md grammar update, and neither new test file (internal/finish/goals_test.go additions, internal/cli/citations_test.go) is present. Requirement coverage for task 5 is 0% in this diff. (For context: docs/takt/sweep-the-open-issue-backlog-fix-the/waves/0/task-5.a1.digest.json records the task-5 attempt as status "blocked" — the implementer reports the core work complete but blocked on a pre-existing fixture in the undeclared file internal/cli/cmd_record_test.go citing a.go:1 in a repo with no a.go — which is presumably why it did not land in this wave's diff. The corresponding code does already exist in the working tree at internal/finish/goals.go:142 (CheckCitations) and internal/cli/cmd_record.go:222, but that is not part of the diff being reviewed here and the task is not marked done.)

follow_ups.title: PlanGate.Reason wiring only exercised indirectly, not through gatherGateFacts
follow_ups.detail: Both SpecGate and PlanGate literals in gatherGateFacts gain `Reason: s.Reason` (lines 135-137 and 143-145). The spec-gate branch is covered end-to-end by TestAnswerRetryOnAnErroredGateWritesNothingAndClearsIt (internal/cli/cmd_answer_retry_test.go), which plants a real error receipt and drives it through gate.Compute → gatherGateFacts → decide → question. The plan-gate branch's Reason threading is only checked via decide_test.go's TestTheGateReviewAskCarriesTheReceiptsReason/plan subtest, which constructs `decide.GateStatus{Verdict: "error", Reason: "x"}` directly and never calls gatherGateFacts or gate.Compute — so a bug specifically in facts.go's plan-gate literal (e.g. a typo omitting `Reason: s.Reason`) would not be caught by any test.

follow_ups.title: Two near-identical 'review errored, retry it' options use different verbs
follow_ups.detail: The new questionGateReviewErrored's retry option is labelled "Re-run the review (Recommended)" (questions.go:166), while the pre-existing questionReviewError (task-review-errored-during-close-wave gate, questions.go:325) uses "Retry the review (Recommended)" for the same underlying concept (a review that errored, offering to run it again). Both use choiceRetry and both are the sole recommended option for an errored review; the label text should match or the divergence should be explained, since a user comparing the two gates has no way to tell the wording difference means anything.

follow_ups.title: Adopted-branch "pr" recommendation label has no test
follow_ups.detail: questionBranchFinish's adopted-branch early return now does `pr.Label += suffixRecommended` (line 409), a new behaviour — before this diff the adopted branch never marked any option "(Recommended)". TestQuestionBranchFinishRecommendsAChoosableOption (internal/decide/finish_test.go) only covers the non-adopted merge-blocked/merge-allowed cases; the existing adopted-branch assertion in TestBranchFinishOptions (finish_test.go:227-232) checks only option order/choice, never the label text. No test would catch a regression that dropped the suffix or duplicated it in the adopted path.

follow_ups.title: Tests do not assert the complete finding-level sequence
follow_ups.detail: reviewRecordLevel returns one matching level, so duplicate or additional review-record findings could pass. Assert levels(fs, "review-record") equals exactly [WARN] or [PASS] as specified.

follow_ups.title: §5.4 still documents FollowUp.Wave as a plain int and the carry as un-de-duplicated, both now false
follow_ups.detail: §5.4 says `gate.FollowUp gains Wave int and Task int, both omitempty` and (line 361-362) `Append-only and un-de-duplicated as before; #44 is untouched by this design and gets more to de-duplicate.` This wave's task 1 changes exactly that: `internal/gate/followup.go` now declares `Wave *int` (nil for a gate follow-up, &n for wave n, so wave 0 serialises as "wave": 0) and `AppendFollowUps` is now idempotent with a Key()-based upgrade rule (approve→override) — i.e. #44 is resolved, not left untouched. The new code comment on the Wave/Task fields even cites this same '§5.4' as its rationale, so the doc it points to now contradicts the shape it documents. No task in this wave updates the two-layers design doc, and it is still an actively cross-referenced document (2026-08-24-takt-design.md links '(two-layers design §5.4)' and similar in several places), so a future reader following that citation is told the wrong field type and the wrong de-duplication story.

follow_ups.title: Newline-flattening fix applied to PriorFindingLines but not to its twin CandidateLines
follow_ups.detail: This diff adds `lineSafe` to collapse newlines in PriorFindingLines' free-text `f.Detail` before rendering one-finding-per-line (brief.go:244), with a doc comment explaining that an unflattened multi-line Detail would 'arrive as several [findings]' to the reviewing agent. CandidateLines (brief.go:202-208), a few lines above in the same file, renders VerifyCandidate.Detail — the same kind of free-form, agent-authored prose (from lens-review findings, wired through cmd_next.go:884) — in the exact same one-per-line format, with the exact same unflattened `c.Detail`. follow_ups.title: plannedTasks' materialised-tasks branch is never verified
follow_ups.detail: plannedTasks(bdir, st) short-circuits to 0 when len(st.Tasks) > 0 (cmd_status.go:178-180), which is exactly the state a normal run is in once it leaves the plan phase (plan.index.json is never deleted after materialiseTasks, so it still sits on disk in execute/finish phase). No test in this diff or pre-existing exercises this branch with an assertion on the tasks/planned output: the new TestStatusPlanPhaseSaysPlannedAndConfirmedClauses only covers the plan-phase case (st.Tasks empty, index present, planned=4); the pre-existing reviewerRun fixture (record_reviewer_test.go:23-49) does set st.Tasks non-empty alongside a real plan.index.json and is used by status tests such as TestStatusInternalReviewSkipped/TestStatusInternalReviewZeroCandidatesNotVerifyPending, but those tests never assert on the 'tasks' or 'planned' fields — so they exercise the line without verifying it. If the early return were dropped (e.g. plannedTasks always parsed the index and returned len(idx.Tasks) whenever it succeeded), every execute/finish-phase status call for a run whose plan.index.json is still on disk would wrongly report 'N planned (not yet materialised)' instead of real task counts, and no test would fail.

follow_ups.title: bundleHint assumes the created-branch convention, ignoring the adopted-branch rule documented next to it
follow_ups.detail: bundleHint's only positive branch guess is `"takt/"+slug` (select.go:122-123), and its doc comment states flatly that `takt init` commits the bundle on takt/<slug>. But cmd_init.go's chooseBranch (internal/cli/cmd_init.go:204-206, spec D9) documents two branch outcomes: on the default branch init creates takt/<slug>, but on any other branch init adopts the current branch (bi.adopted=true) and commits the bundle there instead — under whatever name that branch has, not takt/<slug>. For a run initialised via the adopted path, switching away from that branch and running `status`/`unlock` will fail loadBundle with fs.ErrNotExist, bundleHint's BranchExists(ctx, "takt/"+slug) check will correctly return false (no such branch was ever created), and the code falls through to "no run named <slug> under <base>; check the slug or pass --dir" — telling the user no such run exists when it does, just on a differently-named adopted branch. No existing helper maps a slug back to its actual (possibly adopted) branch, so this is a real gap between the new hint logic and the branch rule the surrounding code already knows about, not just an untested edge case.

follow_ups.title: singleQuoted duplicates the existing shellQuote escaping algorithm
follow_ups.detail: internal/cli/archive.go:353-355 already defines `shellQuote(s string) string { return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", `'\''`) + "'" }` for exactly this POSIX single-quote close-escape-reopen technique, with a comment explaining the same rationale repeated almost verbatim in the new singleQuoted's doc comment (internal/brief/brief.go:265-274). The new PRTitleQuoted (internal/brief/brief.go:275-281) reimplements the same one-line escaping rule in a different package instead of sharing it, so a future fix or hardening of the shell-escaping rule (e.g. for control characters) has two independent copies to update.

follow_ups.title: Body path interpolated unquoted in the same shell command whose title is carefully quoted
follow_ups.detail: `gh pr create --base {{.Base}} --title '{{.PRTitleQuoted}}' --body-file {{.PRBodyPath}}` quotes the title (via singleQuoted/PRTitleQuoted, added specifically because a shell would otherwise split the command on spaces) but leaves `--body-file {{.PRBodyPath}}` bare. PRBodyPath is finish.PRPath(bdir), an absolute path under the workspace/repo root, which can contain spaces just as much as any other filesystem path — the exact risk internal/cli/archive.go's shellQuote (used for discardSweep's `git clean -fd -- '<rel>'`) exists to guard against ('a worktree path is whatever the user's filesystem says — a space in it would otherwise split the command into arguments'). brief.go:279-280 asserts PRBodyPath is safe to interpolate bare 'since it is takt's own <bundle>/finish/pr.md', but that reasoning is exactly what shellQuote's own doc comment rejects for repo/bundle-relative paths. The same command should quote both arguments.

follow_ups.title: Malformed external bundles receive impossible Git recovery advice

Use repository-aware guidance, such as restoring from Git only for in-repository bundles and repairing/restoring the named file otherwise.
